stories.title: Hackers hit shop freezers in seven European countries, spoiling food worth millions
stories.deck: A suspected cyber-attack set supermarket refrigeration units to defrost overnight, a month after a similar attack in France.
summary: Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries woke on Monday to refrigerators and freezers that had been quietly switched into defrost mode. Around 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, along with a smaller number of shops in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Local media reported that food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away.

Sabcobel, the Belgian firm that manufactures some of the units and runs Delhaize's systems, called it a cyber-attack. Its chief executive, Stephan Moelans, said staff had worked through the night to disconnect affected units from the network. He said the method appeared to match last month's attack on hundreds of French supermarkets. In some shops, freezer temperatures reportedly climbed as high as 50C. One Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told a Belgian news site it had lost about €100,000 of produce.

The spread of the damage varied by chain. Carrefour said 15 of its Belgian stores were hit but stayed open. Colruyt, which franchises Spar shops, reported five affected. In Sweden, several ICA and seven of 800 Coop stores were hit. In Ireland, 13 SuperValu stores were affected, though owner Musgrave said only a specific refrigerator model was involved. Danfoss, a Danish manufacturer, told Dutch radio that at least 17 Dutch businesses were hit, mostly butchers and small neighbourhood shops.

TechCrunch reports that security researchers have tied the French incidents to internet-connected Danfoss controllers that no longer received security updates, and that the security firm Claroty warned in August that such units could be hacked remotely. Moelans said the fix needs physical changes to the units, not only software updates, and that many customers moved to a secure connection after the French attack.

Nobody has been identified as responsible. Belgium's and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the situation, and the UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with partners. No incidents have been reported in the UK.

stories.title: Binance customers pull $3.6bn as exchange reopens after record hack
stories.deck: Withdrawals resumed in phases on Sunday while Binance says it has covered about 95% of the $6.3bn stolen.
summary: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, reopened withdrawals on Sunday and saw a rush for the exit. Between 06:00 and 15:30 GMT it processed $4.649bn of withdrawals against $1.01bn of deposits, a net outflow of about $3.64bn. The firm said that was just over 2% of the $171bn it holds for customers, that the initial spike had eased, and that flows were "stabilising as expected".

The reopening follows what is believed to be the largest hack in history. About $6.3bn of digital assets were taken from Binance's global exchange; its US-facing platform says it was not affected. The FBI said on Saturday that a North Korean group known as TraderTraitor, also called the Lazarus Group, was responsible, and published wallet addresses linked to it, asking industry partners to block transactions involving them. The same group was blamed for the $1.5bn Bybit theft in 2025.

Binance says it has replaced around 95% of the stolen assets using its corporate treasury, a futures insurance fund and emergency reserves, and that the rest are harder to buy at scale. It has promised that losses "will not be passed on to users". Early checks suggest the breach may have begun with a compromised laptop belonging to an engineer, the company said, and a fuller incident report will follow.

Recovery looks difficult. Alec Zebrick of the analytics firm Chainalysis, which is helping Binance and governments, said the attackers are laundering the money "quite actively" across thousands of addresses. TechCrunch reports the FBI believes the funds are being converted mainly into Ethereum. Binance says withdrawals for more than two dozen major coins are open, but status varies by network: Bitcoin withdrawals were still listed as partially suspended on Sunday morning. Users should expect delays.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly cuts its fundraising target to $20bn as investors turn cautious
stories.deck: Reports say the AI company has secured about $11bn so far, well short of earlier ambitions.
summary: OpenAI's latest funding round is reportedly falling short of what the company first hoped for. According to TechCrunch, which is relaying reports from the Financial Times and the Wall Street Journal, the company has lowered its target to $20bn. OpenAI has not confirmed the figures, and TechCrunch said it had asked the company for comment.

The target has moved a long way in a few weeks. In late September the company was reported to be seeking $30bn at a $1.4 trillion valuation. By late October the reported valuation had slipped to $1.25 trillion, with an initial public offering said to be planned. The Financial Times now says the first close will be smaller than the $20bn goal.

The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI has secured roughly $11bn so far, less than half of the original $30bn, and that some large investors responded with a "tepid" reception. The Financial Times says investors from the United Arab Emirates are leading the round, and that a later offering to wealthy individuals could lift the total to $20bn.

TechCrunch ties the softer demand partly to timing. Wall Street has grown wary of heavy spending on AI infrastructure, which has contributed to a sell-off in technology shares, and Anthropic's planned public listing may also face difficulties. For readers, the main point is that the reported numbers come from secondary accounts of private negotiations and could change before any round closes.

stories.title: Apple's new chief says the company won't "ship AI for AI's sake"
stories.deck: John Ternus defended Apple's measured pace on artificial intelligence in an interview with Wired.
summary: Apple's chief executive, John Ternus, has pushed back on the idea that the company is behind in artificial intelligence. In an interview with Wired's Steven Levy, reported by TechCrunch, he said "everyone has an opinion" about Apple's position, but "I really like where we're at."

The context matters. Apple has often been described as lagging in AI over the past couple of years, and it delayed a more powerful version of Siri that finally launched this summer, on 3 August. Ternus, a longtime Apple executive, took over as chief executive at the start of September.

He insisted that Apple will use AI heavily in new products. "We don't want to ship AI for AI's sake," he said. "When we're doing it right, people won't have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?"

Asked whether AI agents could change Apple's ecosystem more sharply, perhaps by making apps unnecessary, Ternus conceded that this "could make life really easy, I suppose". He added that creating products "is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do."

These are the executive's own statements, not independent assessments of Apple's AI progress. They suggest the company intends to keep AI in the background rather than market it as a headline feature.

stories.title: Shah and the opposition trade charges over India's voter-roll revision
stories.deck: A mass Delhi rally demanded the election chief's resignation; the home minister answered with claims about "infiltrators" that the reporting does not independently verify.
summary: India's dispute over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls sharpened this weekend. On Sunday, tens of thousands of supporters of the opposition INDIA bloc gathered at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, chanting "Save the vote, save the country". Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi were joined by Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Mehbooba Mufti and others. Kharge said the campaign would continue until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns.

The BBC reports that more than 130 million names have been removed from draft rolls. The Election Commission says the exercise removes duplicates and people who have died, moved or are ineligible, and that wrongly excluded voters can seek restoration. The opposition says eligible voters are being deleted to help the BJP. The BJP and the Commission deny that. JP Nadda called the rally a "calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy".

On Monday at a Hyderabad rally, Home Minister Amit Shah, according to the Indian Express, said the rally aimed to protect "infiltrators" and claimed three crore deleted entries were Bangladeshi infiltrators who "never existed". He called Rahul Gandhi's figure of 13 crore deletions a lie, saying 6.15 crore people had moved, 2.8 to 3 crore had died and one crore were duplicates. He challenged Gandhi to a special parliamentary session on SIR, infiltrators and EVMs.

These are political claims. The reports do not independently confirm the "infiltrator" figures, and the numbers offered by each side do not reconcile. The Indian Express reported in September that Kumar made key decisions over objections from two fellow commissioners, which the Commission said did not affect its functioning.

stories.title: Cyclone Murasu nears Andhra coast as Odisha and Tamil Nadu move teams
stories.deck: Landfall is expected between Nellore and Narasapur around midnight, the second eastern-coast cyclone in a week.
summary: Less than a week after Cyclone Arnab, a second storm is bearing down on India's eastern coast. According to the India Meteorological Department, severe cyclonic storm Murasu was moving at 14 km/h and sat about 110 km from Nellore on Monday. It is expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narasapur, south of Ongole, between about 11:30 pm Monday and 4 am Tuesday, with winds of 100 to 110 km/h and gusts up to 120 km/h.

Extremely heavy rain is likely at one or two places in Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore, Chittoor and Tirupati districts. Officials told Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu that Palnadu could see about 30 cm, Prakasam 24 cm and Markapuram 19 cm. Naidu told officials to prevent loss of life and property, use the rain to fill tanks and reservoirs, and finish post-cyclone restoration within 48 hours. Schools have closed in parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

Odisha has put southern districts on high alert. Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said evacuations from low-lying areas had begun in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal, and that more than 300 rescue teams from the NDRF, ODRAF and fire service were pre-positioned. Tamil Nadu is sending 500 electricity workers in 25 teams after Naidu asked Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay for help with damaged power poles. Three NDRF teams of 90 personnel have been deployed from Arakkonam.
West Bengal has no warning but may see light rain on 3 and 4 November. The figures above are forecasts and official statements from Monday afternoon and may change as the storm moves.

stories.title: India signs ₹53,866 crore deals for eight Navy-designed corvettes
stories.deck: Garden Reach and Goa Shipyard will build the ships, in a project the defence ministry calls a milestone for indigenous warship design.
summary: The Ministry of Defence on Monday signed contracts worth ₹53,866.50 crore for eight next-generation corvettes for the Indian Navy. Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh was present for the signing in New Delhi. The Cabinet Committee on Security had cleared the project days earlier.

Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Limited will build five of the ships and Goa Shipyard Limited the remaining three. The ministry says it is the first project in which ships designed by the Indian Navy itself will be built by defence public-sector companies chosen through a competitive process. The corvettes will complement the Navy's four existing Kamorta-class corvettes.

According to the ministry, the vessels will carry advanced missiles, weapons and sensors for operations in the air, on the surface and below it. It lists their roles as anti-submarine warfare, maritime surveillance and reconnaissance, search-and-attack missions, coastal and littoral defence, and protecting trade routes.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on X that construction would generate roughly 72 lakh person-days of work in shipyards and 460 lakh person-days in supplier industries and small firms over ten years. The ministry says the order will strengthen cooperation between public shipyards, private yards and industrial partners.

The Defence Acquisition Council first approved the need for the project in June 2022 at an estimated cost of about ₹36,000 crore. The final contract value is therefore well above that early estimate. These are the ministry's own claims about capability and employment, and they have not been independently assessed.

stories.title: New rules let the Centre direct airfares in "extraordinary" situations
stories.deck: The aviation rules also require airlines to file tariffs and show a full fare breakdown, but stop short of a price cap.
summary: The government can now issue written directions to airlines on fares when it judges that the public interest requires it. The power sits in new rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, which were notified on the e-Gazette on 31 October. The Hindu describes the framework as one of enhanced monitoring and transparency rather than a fare cap.

The rules require airlines to submit tariffs to the Director General of Civil Aviation in the form, manner and intervals the regulator specifies, and to publish them on their websites or other platforms the DGCA names. Fares shown on booking sites and tickets must state the total payable, with a breakdown of base fare, taxes, fees, cancellation charges and refund conditions.

Intervention is not new. The Centre imposed fare bands during the Covid-19 pandemic and after IndiGo's operational breakdown last December, when nearly 5,000 flights were cancelled. It has also informally urged restraint during the Kumbh Mela, after the Pahalgam attacks and during natural disasters such as the Kerala floods. Airlines were already expected to file fare data under a 2010 circular.

The official position remains that airfares are market-driven, following the repeal of the Air Corporations Act in March 1994. The Hindu notes a public-interest petition by activist S. Laxminarayan seeking binding norms against arbitrary fares and add-on charges at festival times and in emergencies. The new rules do not define "extraordinary situations", so how often the power is used will depend on future decisions.

stories.title: Delhi air turns "very poor" at AQI 324; Stage-II GRAP invoked across NCR
stories.deck: The pollution regulator tightened curbs after air quality worsened sharply in two days.
summary: Delhi's air has deteriorated quickly. The Hindu reports that the city's air quality index rose from 117, in the "moderate" band, on 31 October to 261 ("poor") on 1 November and then to 324 on Monday, which falls in the "very poor" category of 301 to 400. The Central Pollution Control Board labels 401 to 500 "severe".

In response, the Commission for Air Quality Management's sub-committee on the Graded Response Action Plan invoked Stage-II across the National Capital Region on Monday. It cited unfavourable weather and forecasts from the India Meteorological Department and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology. The commission ordered every agency in the region to implement Stage-II actions "with immediate effect in right earnest", in addition to the Stage-I measures already in force.

Stage-II tells NCR state governments to raise parking fees to discourage private vehicle use. The Delhi government and neighbouring states must stagger office timings for public bodies and municipal agencies in Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar. Existing measures such as mechanical road sweeping and water sprinkling must be applied more strictly.

Weather figures from Monday show a maximum of 29.5C at Safdarjung, one degree below normal, and a minimum of 16.4C, 1.1 degrees above normal. No rain was recorded at any station in the 24 hours to 5:30 pm. The reports do not say when conditions are expected to improve.

stories.title: Ukrainian and Russian alert apps hacked to send fake nuclear warnings
stories.deck: Both countries say their emergency apps were compromised on Sunday night; officials say there was no real threat.
summary: Ukraine and Russia both said on Sunday night that their emergency alert apps had been hacked and used to send false warnings, including of nuclear attack. Ukraine's Air Alert app, supported by the Ministry of Digital Transformation, pushed red-level air-raid warnings across the country shortly before 23:00 local time. Messages claimed a radiation threat in Kyiv, a chemical-attack risk and street fighting, one reading "it's Oreshnik flying", a reference to a Russian intermediate-range missile.

Ukrainian officials moved quickly to reassure the public. "There is no radiation threat! Stay calm," the app's Telegram channel said. All-clear messages followed around 23:53. The ministry said the app had "apparently been compromised" and was temporarily disabled. Oleksandr Merezhko, who chairs parliament's foreign affairs committee, said the attack caused no panic, partly because the message was in Russian, which aroused suspicion, and because Kyiv residents are used to constant alerts.

Hours later, Russia's emergencies ministry said its own app had suffered "a massive cyberattack" that sent fake information to the public. It said the incident could not affect the national alert system, which uses sirens, loudspeakers, texts, television and radio. Ukrainian media, citing the partisan group Atesh, reported that the Russian-side messages falsely warned of nuclear strikes. The BBC could not independently verify who carried out either attack.

Herbert Lin of Stanford University said it was likely the first such hack of an official Ukrainian information app and "I suspect it won't be the last". The alerts came minutes before a local ceasefire in the Kherson region, meant to let civilians leave Oleshky, expired at 23:00.

stories.title: Cost-of-living protests turn violent in German cities as unrest spreads across Europe
stories.deck: Shops were looted in Frankfurt and police were injured in Berlin after largely peaceful youth marches on Saturday.
summary: Protests over the cost of living turned violent in several German cities on Saturday night. Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt, and clashes were reported in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. Police used water cannon against people who threw fireworks, stones and bottles at emergency workers. Earlier in the day, thousands had joined mostly peaceful marches organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt, which objects to school underfunding, high living costs, spending cuts and military service.

In Frankfurt, police reported "violent riots", smashed windows and petrol bombs thrown at emergency services. A gun shop was damaged and two weapons recovered. Hesse's interior minister, Roman Poseck, said around 100 "clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest. In Berlin, 27 officers were injured and up to 56 people briefly detained. Broadcaster NDR reported 120 arrests in Hamburg. Authorities counted as many as 18,000 protesters in three cities, about half the organisers' estimate.

Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrators wanted "peace and freedom, rather than war and coercion". Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called for harsh punishment of rioters and said police had prevented "violence like that seen in Paris".

The unrest follows youth-led protests elsewhere. In France, more than 320,000 people marched on Saturday in a third weekend of mostly peaceful demonstrations, and the interior ministry reported over 770 arrests. A police officer was hurt by a petrol bomb, prompting an attempted-murder inquiry. Protests also took place in Italy and Portugal, where housing costs are central.

stories.title: Ebola has killed more than 5,000 in DR Congo, the country's worst outbreak
stories.deck: Government data show over 10,300 confirmed cases across eight provinces, with attacks on health workers complicating the response.
summary: More than 5,000 people have died in an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to government data cited by the BBC. Over 10,300 cases have been confirmed across eight of the country's 26 provinces, and the case fatality rate stands at 48.6%. The outbreak began in May and became the country's deadliest in history in August. The epicentre remains Ituri province in the north-east.

The United Nations says it is the 17th outbreak in the country and the second largest ever. It is driven by the Bundibugyo species. The previous worst outbreak in Congo killed 2,299 people between 2018 and 2020. The deadliest on record was in West Africa from 2014 to 2016, with more than 11,325 deaths, according to the World Health Organization. The UN warns that the current outbreak is "taking lives at a much faster rate".

Cases have crossed borders. Uganda reported 20 cases and two deaths early on, with none since August. Kenya has nine confirmed cases and two deaths. Nigeria identified two suspected cases on Saturday; earlier in October a woman confirmed with the disease there was flown to Switzerland for treatment. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control rates the risk to people in Europe as "very low".

Violence is hampering the response. Radio Okapi reported that a nurse was killed and a health worker seriously injured this week when local youths accused them of contaminating water. Last month a politician was beaten to death after promoting prevention measures. The WHO's Africa office has called for more control measures, access to affected areas and community outreach.

stories.title: Nine killed as small jet crashes onto a Florida road near Palm Beach
stories.deck: The Learjet went down in heavy weather on Sunday; no one on the ground was hurt, and the NTSB is investigating.
summary: Nine people died on Sunday when a Learjet 60 crashed onto a busy road in Palm Beach County, Florida, about nine miles from President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort. The crash, at around 12:50 pm local time, happened on Military Trail, a six-lane road lined with businesses and restaurants. Nobody on the ground was hurt, officials said, though Palm Beach County Fire Rescue declared a mass-casualty incident.

The Federal Aviation Administration said the aircraft had left Austin, Texas, for the Bahamas. Flight analysis suggested it was plunging steeply before impact. Air traffic control audio, as described by the BBC, included reports of "moderate turbulence" and the crew "managing the ice". A crew member later declared an emergency, saying the aircraft was in an overspeed condition and descending at 20,000 feet a minute. The last remark, about 35 seconds after the first mayday, was "we're out of time".

Thunderstorms had been reported in the area. The cause has not been determined. The FAA is sending a team to assist the National Transportation Safety Board, which leads the investigation. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called it a "horrific tragedy".

Governor Ron DeSantis and local officials said about 600 residents of a nearby trailer park were being evacuated. Damage to infrastructure, including water lines, means the road will stay closed for at least 30 days. Trump had left a nearby airport on Air Force One about an hour before the crash.

stories.title: Judge throws out Trump's libel suit against the Wall Street Journal
stories.deck: A federal judge ruled the Epstein birthday-letter case could not meet the "actual malice" standard and dismissed it with prejudice.
summary: A US federal judge has dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and its parent company Dow Jones. Judge Darrin Gayles ruled "with prejudice", meaning the case cannot be filed again. In a 20-page ruling he wrote that the suit was "grasping at straws" to "manufacture flaws" in the paper's reporting, and that it ran counter to the First Amendment.

The case concerned a story about a 2003 birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein that appeared to carry Trump's signature. According to the BBC, the letter contained suggestive language and a drawing of the outline of a woman's body. Trump said last year that he did not write or sign it, called it fake, and sued Dow Jones and Rupert Murdoch, first seeking $20bn and later $10bn. These are his claims. The court did not rule on whether the letter is genuine.

Gayles found that Trump's lawyers had not shown the defendants published defamatory statements with "actual malice", which the law requires of public figures. He rejected the argument that the paper should have disregarded its investigation because Trump denied writing the letter. That reasoning, he wrote, "is not what the actual malice standard requires and runs afoul of the First Amendment". If it were the law, journalists could be blocked from publishing whenever a public figure denied an accusation.
The judge also noted the paper's "thoughtful and detailed investigation". The BBC does not say whether Trump will appeal.

stories.title: Antonelli becomes Formula 1's youngest world champion in Mexico
stories.deck: The Mercedes driver clinched the title with third place at 20 years and 68 days old, as Verstappen won the race.
summary: Kimi Antonelli has won the Formula 1 world championship, finishing third in the Mexico City Grand Prix to seal the title at 20 years and 68 days old. That makes him the youngest champion in the sport's history, beating Sebastian Vettel's record by three years and 66 days. He is also the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. "Thank you so much. We did it. We did it," he said.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race, ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, with Antonelli third. Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari, followed by Lando Norris, George Russell, Oscar Piastri, Franco Colapinto, Liam Lawson and Pierre Gasly. A red flag, after Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac crashed on lap 45 when its front suspension failed under braking, led to a 25-lap sprint to the finish.

Other incidents shaped the order. Russell received a 10-second penalty for tipping Red Bull's Isack Hadjar into a spin on the first lap, and Leclerc a five-second penalty for his own first-lap incident. Arvid Lindblad crashed his Racing Bulls after a collision with Piastri with 12 laps to go. BBC Sport notes that Antonelli was still a teenager until late August.
He leads the standings by 43 points after five races, according to the report. The next round is the Sao Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos from 6 to 8 November.

stories.title: Hamilton says Ferrari need "serious talks" after Leclerc clash cost them a win
stories.deck: Lewis Hamilton said the team lost a possible one-two in Mexico because its drivers fought each other.
summary: Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari must have "some serious talks behind closed doors" after a first-lap fight with team-mate Charles Leclerc cost the team victory in Mexico City. Hamilton took his first pole position for Ferrari but finished second to Max Verstappen, with Leclerc fourth after a penalty. During the red-flag period Hamilton said over the radio: "We've got big problems. Big, big problems."

Hamilton's account is that the two Ferraris were running first and second into Turn Four when Leclerc pushed him wide, and that the team "could have easily had a one-two" with its pace. He called Leclerc's move "unnecessary" and said "we don't have rules of engagement", adding that "something needs to change for sure". Of Leclerc, who is 28, he said: "I think it's a mentality thing. It's like do or die, either I win or none of us do, and it shouldn't be that."

Leclerc, who cut a chicane on the first lap, said he would speak with Hamilton. He argued that with a Red Bull second he felt it was worth keeping the position, and added that he could also be unhappy about how far he was pushed off track out of Turn One, "but it is racing". Team principal Frederic Vasseur said he was frustrated, mainly for the 2,000 people working on the project, and that the team would discuss it that night.

Verstappen said Ferrari "made it a little bit difficult for themselves fighting each other". BBC Sport calls it the latest and arguably most serious of several tensions between the drivers this season, including incidents at the Italian Grand Prix and a tyre dispute in Singapore. All of this is the drivers' own account.
